1	import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
2	import type { NextRequest } from "next/server";
3	
4	/**
5	 * CSP proxy (Next.js 16 renamed Middleware → Proxy) with per-request nonces.
6	 *
7	 * Why nonces + 'strict-dynamic': only scripts that Next.js has explicitly
8	 * tagged with the nonce can run, and any scripts they load inherit trust.
9	 * This keeps a hypothetical injected `<script>` tag from executing even if
10	 * something slipped past markdown sanitization.
11	 *
12	 * Why `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`: many React components use inline
13	 * `style={{...}}` props (e.g. proof-graph node positioning, refinement
14	 * preview, collapsible sections), and Next.js's SSR style injection also
15	 * emits inline <style> tags. Tightening to nonces would require auditing
16	 * every such site. Documented as a deliberate carve-out, not an oversight.
17	 *
18	 * `connect-src 'self'` is sufficient because Anthropic / OpenAlex / OpenRouter
19	 * calls are server-to-server (Next API routes), not browser-to-third-party.
20	 *
21	 * Why `allowUnsafeEval` in development only: Next.js's dev server (HMR + eval
22	 * source maps) injects `eval()`-based code that a strict CSP blocks, flooding
23	 * the browser console with EvalErrors. Production output is genuinely
24	 * eval-free, so `'unsafe-eval'` is added only when NODE_ENV !== "production".
25	 */
26	export function buildCsp(
27	  nonce: string,
28	  allowUnsafeEval: boolean = process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production",
29	): string {
30	  const scriptSrc = `script-src 'self' 'nonce-${nonce}' 'strict-dynamic'${
31	    allowUnsafeEval ? " 'unsafe-eval'" : ""
32	  }`;
33	  const directives = [
34	    "default-src 'self'",
35	    scriptSrc,
36	    "style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'",
37	    "img-src 'self' data: blob:",
38	    "font-src 'self' data:",
39	    "connect-src 'self'",
40	    "frame-ancestors 'none'",
41	    "base-uri 'self'",
42	    "object-src 'none'",
43	    // form-action does NOT fall back to default-src (CSP3); set explicitly.
44	    "form-action 'self'",
45	  ];
46	  return directives.join("; ");
47	}
48	
49	export function proxy(request: NextRequest): NextResponse {
50	  // Generate a fresh 128-bit nonce per request. crypto.getRandomValues + Buffer
51	  // are both available in the Node.js runtime Next 16 Proxy runs on by default.
52	  const nonce = Buffer.from(crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(16))).toString("base64");
53	  const csp = buildCsp(nonce);
54	
55	  // Forward the nonce to server components via a request header so layouts
56	  // can read it via `headers()` and pass it to <Script> tags they render.
57	  // Setting CSP on both the forwarded request and the response matches the
58	  // canonical Next.js docs example.
59	  const requestHeaders = new Headers(request.headers);
60	  requestHeaders.set("x-nonce", nonce);
61	  requestHeaders.set("Content-Security-Policy", csp);
62	
63	  const response = NextResponse.next({
64	    request: { headers: requestHeaders },
65	  });
66	  response.headers.set("Content-Security-Policy", csp);
67	  return response;
68	}
69	
70	export const config = {
71	  // Apply CSP to page navigations only. Skip API routes (they don't render
72	  // HTML), Next's static assets (no scripts to nonce), and prefetches (which
73	  // would otherwise burn a nonce on a request that may never paint).
74	  matcher: [
75	    {
76	      source: "/((?!api|_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico).*)",
77	      missing: [
78	        { type: "header", key: "next-router-prefetch" },
79	        { type: "header", key: "purpose", value: "prefetch" },
80	      ],
81	    },
82	  ],
83	};

1	import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
2	import type { NextRequest } from "next/server";
3	
4	/**
5	 * CSP proxy (Next.js 16 renamed Middleware → Proxy) with per-request nonces.
6	 *
7	 * Why nonces + 'strict-dynamic': only scripts that Next.js has explicitly
8	 * tagged with the nonce can run, and any scripts they load inherit trust.
9	 * This keeps a hypothetical injected `<script>` tag from executing even if
10	 * something slipped past markdown sanitization.
11	 *
12	 * Why `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`: many React components use inline
13	 * `style={{...}}` props (e.g. proof-graph node positioning, refinement
14	 * preview, collapsible sections), and Next.js's SSR style injection also
15	 * emits inline <style> tags. Tightening to nonces would require auditing
16	 * every such site. Documented as a deliberate carve-out, not an oversight.
17	 *
18	 * `connect-src 'self'` is sufficient because Anthropic / OpenAlex / OpenRouter
19	 * calls are server-to-server (Next API routes), not browser-to-third-party.
20	 *
21	 * Why `allowUnsafeEval` in development only: Next.js's dev server (HMR + eval
22	 * source maps) injects `eval()`-based code that a strict CSP blocks, flooding
23	 * the browser console with EvalErrors. Production output is genuinely
24	 * eval-free, so `'unsafe-eval'` is added only when NODE_ENV !== "production".
25	 */
26	export function buildCsp(
27	  nonce: string,
28	  allowUnsafeEval: boolean = process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production",
29	): string {
30	  const scriptSrc = `script-src 'self' 'nonce-${nonce}' 'strict-dynamic'${
31	    allowUnsafeEval ? " 'unsafe-eval'" : ""
32	  }`;
33	  const directives = [
34	    "default-src 'self'",
35	    scriptSrc,
36	    "style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'",
37	    "img-src 'self' data: blob:",
38	    "font-src 'self' data:",
39	    "connect-src 'self'",
40	    "frame-ancestors 'none'",
41	    "base-uri 'self'",
42	    "object-src 'none'",
43	    // form-action does NOT fall back to default-src (CSP3); set explicitly.
44	    "form-action 'self'",
45	  ];
46	  return directives.join("; ");
47	}
48	
49	export function proxy(request: NextRequest): NextResponse {
50	  // Generate a fresh 128-bit nonce per request. crypto.getRandomValues + Buffer
51	  // are both available in the Node.js runtime Next 16 Proxy runs on by default.
52	  const nonce = Buffer.from(crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(16))).toString("base64");
53	  const csp = buildCsp(nonce);
54	
55	  // Forward the nonce to server components via a request header so layouts
56	  // can read it via `headers()` and pass it to <Script> tags they render.
57	  // Setting CSP on both the forwarded request and the response matches the
58	  // canonical Next.js docs example.
59	  const requestHeaders = new Headers(request.headers);
60	  requestHeaders.set("x-nonce", nonce);
61	  requestHeaders.set("Content-Security-Policy", csp);
62	
63	  const response = NextResponse.next({
64	    request: { headers: requestHeaders },
65	  });
66	  response.headers.set("Content-Security-Policy", csp);
67	  return response;
68	}

- Summary: `allowUnsafeEval: boolean = process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"` is a default-parameter expression, so `process.env.NODE_ENV` is read and compared on every call to `buildCsp`, which `proxy()` (line 53) invokes once per matched request. `NODE_ENV` cannot change over a process's lifetime, so this is a per-request re-computation of a process-lifetime constant. `process.env` reads in Node are proxied lookups, noticeably slower than a plain const read.
- Failure scenario: every non-prefetch page navigation through the proxy pays a redundant env lookup + comparison. The cost is microseconds — this is a middleware hot path but the absolute waste is tiny; it's a cleanliness/idiom issue more than a measurable regression.

All files read and analyzed. Dependencies aren't installed in this checkout (`node_modules` missing), so I verified test behavior statically rather than by running vitest. Here are my findings. ## Candidate findings **1. `proxy.test.ts:33` — the `http:` scheme assertion is vacuous; it can never match a real CSP scheme source** `expect(csp).not.toMatch(/\bhttp:\b/)`. The trailing `\b` requires a word/non-word transition after the `:`, but `:` is a non-word character, and in any real CSP the token `http:` is followed by a space, end-of-string, or `/` (as in `http://evil.com`) — all non-word. So there is no word boundary and the regex matches nothing. Failure scenario: change `img-src 'self' data: blob:` to `img-src http: data:` (or add `connect-src http://evil.com`) — this "does not allow ... http: schemes in production" test still passes, silently shipping a plaintext-scheme CSP allowance. Fix: `/http:/` or `/\bhttp:/` (leading `\b` alone works since `h` is a word char). This line is pre-existing but sits inside the it-block this diff renamed and re-scoped, so the review touched it while leaving the assertion broken. **2. `proxy.ts:28` — `allowUnsafeEval` default is fail-open: any NODE_ENV other than exactly `"production"` gets `'unsafe-eval'`** Default is `process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"`. (Default parameters are evaluated per call, not at module load, so the timing itself is fine — the caller `proxy()` at line 53 calls `buildCsp(nonce)` with the ambient env each request.) But the predicate allows eval for `"test"`, `"staging"`, `"preview"`, and crucially *unset* NODE_ENV. Failure scenario: a self-hosted deployment (the README's non-Vercel path, or a custom `node` server wrapping the built app) that doesn't export NODE_ENV serves end users a CSP containing `'unsafe-eval'`, quietly weakening the exact XSS defense this proxy exists for. Fail-closed would be `=== "development"` (matching the comment's own claim, "development only"). The prod test at line 12 pins `buildCsp(NONCE, false)` so no test would catch this misconfiguration at runtime. **3. `app/components/panels/BalancedPerspectivesPanel.tsx:113-117` — `t.between &&` doesn't guard a *partial* tuple; a length-1 array renders a dangling `↔` arrow** The regression being fixed came from partial-JSON streaming, and the same partial-JSON parser that omits `between` entirely can also emit it half-built: `between: ["Perspective A"]` (second element not yet streamed). The guard passes, `t.between[1]` is `undefined`, and the panel renders `Perspective A ↔` with an empty right endpoint mid-stream. Not a crash, but the same streaming state the fix targets still produces visibly broken UI. A `t.between?.length === 2` (or `t.between?.[1] != null`) guard would cover both cases. The new test only covers `between` absent, not partial. **4. `app/components/panels/BalancedPerspectivesPanel.tsx:70` (and `:137`) — streaming-unsafe React keys: `key={p.id}` / `key={h.perspectiveId}` are `undefined` for partially-streamed items** Same partial-stream class of bug as the one fixed, one section up in the same component. Failure scenario: the last directive is weakened to `form-action *` (or a future directive appended at the end with a bare `*`) — the "does not allow ... wildcards" test passes. `/\*(\s|$)/` (or splitting into tokens) closes the gap. Review complete. I ran `git diff main...HEAD`, read the panel, the proxy, the artifact types, and traced the streaming producer chain (`useArtifactGeneration` → `partial-json` → `page.tsx` casts → panels via `mergeStreamingPreview`/`useStreamingMerge`).

## Mechanism (context for findings)

The streamed preview is parsed by `partial-json` into `unknown` (`/repo/app/hooks/useArtifactGeneration.ts:75-84`, stored as `Partial<Record<ArtifactType, unknown>>`), then cast in `/repo/app/page.tsx:951-994 `to the **fully-complete** artifact types (e.g. `as BalancedPerspectivesResponse["balancedPerspectives"]`). So inside every panel, `displayMap` is typed as complete — including `between: [string, string]` at `/repo/app/lib/types/artifacts.ts:100` — while the runtime value can be arbitrarily partial. The types lie, the compiler can't flag a missing guard, and safety depends on each panel author remembering `?.`.

## Findings (3)

1. **`/repo/app/components/panels/BalancedPerspectivesPanel.tsx:113`** — The `{t.between && ...}` guard fixes one field of one panel while the underlying mechanism guarantees the same crash class everywhere.
   *failure_scenario:* Because streamed partials are cast to complete types at `page.tsx:951-994`, the next unguarded access is a runtime TypeError the compiler never sees — and one already exists (finding 2). Typing the preview prop as `DeepPartial<T>` (or validating at the parse boundary in `useArtifactGeneration`) would turn every such site into a compile error; the panels' pervasive hand-written `?.`/truthy guards show the convention is voluntary and leak-prone. This guard is correct locally, but it's whack-a-mole depth.

2. **`/repo/app/components/panels/CausalGraphPanel.tsx:53-95, 24-30`** — Live instance of the identical crash class in the sibling panel's Details view, fed by the same streaming preview (`useStreamingMerge` at :114, `displayGraph` passed to `DetailsView` at :172).
   *failure_scenario:* User switches to "Details" view, then regenerates: mid-stream, `causalGraph.edges.length` (:69), `causalGraph.confounders.length` (:87), `c.affectedEdges.join(", ")` (:95), and `WeightBadge`'s `weight.toFixed(2)` (:30, on an edge whose `weight` hasn't streamed) each throw and crash the panel. Notably, the graph view is already explicitly hardened against exactly this — `/repo/app/components/features/causal-graph/useCausalGraphLayout.ts:43-55` has `?? []` fallbacks and the comment "missing weight causes .toFixed() to throw" — proving the hazard is known but fixed per-view, not at the boundary. This is concrete evidence for finding 1 that the crash class is not "already done elsewhere."

3. **`/repo/app/components/panels/BalancedPerspectivesPanel.tsx:113-117`** (minor) — The truthiness guard doesn't match the tuple invariant: `partial-json` can yield `between: ["A"]` mid-stream, which passes `t.between &&` and renders a dangling "A ↔ " with an empty right endpoint.
   *failure_scenario:* Cosmetic flicker only (no crash — `undefined` renders as empty). `t.between?.length === 2` would honor the `[string, string]` type. Worth folding into whichever fix addresses finding 1; not worth a standalone change.

## Checked and not flagged

- **`proxy.ts` unsafe-eval toggle** (`/repo/proxy.ts:26-32`): appropriate depth, no concrete fragility found. The conditional is scoped to a single directive; the `allowUnsafeEval` parameter with a `NODE_ENV` default makes tests deterministic (`proxy.test.ts` pins `buildCsp(NONCE, false)` and asserts exactly one `'unsafe-eval'` occurrence, preventing silent leakage into other directives). Vercel preview/prod builds run with `NODE_ENV=production`, so the dev carve-out can't reach deployments. A separate dev/prod CSP would duplicate nine directives to vary one token — worse, not better.
- **StatisticalModelPanel / PropertyTestsPanel**: consistently use the `(x?.length ?? 0) > 0` guard-then-access pattern; no unguarded partial access found.
- The evidence-search and evidenceStore hunks are comment-only; the duplicated merge helper (`mergeStreamingPreview.ts` vs `useStreamingMerge.ts`) predates this branch and is out of scope.
- The new test file correctly pins the regression (casts a `between`-less tension past the lying type — itself a small signal for finding 1).
